01-umaid-bhawan-palace-jodhpur.title: Umaid Bhawan Palace: Where Art Deco Meets Rajput Grandeur

images.subject: Palace exterior panorama from eastern approach
images.caption: Umaid Bhawan Palace, Jodhpur
images.imageDetail: The palace's golden sandstone, quarried from local Chittar stone, was transported by camel cart across sixteen years of construction.
images.altText: Umaid Bhawan Palace exterior — golden sandstone palace rising from Chittar Hill in Jodhpur

images.subject: Central dome and cupola
images.caption: The central dome and cupola, Umaid Bhawan Palace
images.imageDetail: Henry Lanchester's design synthesises the Sanchi stupa's hemispherical dome and the Taj Mahal's proportions with Art Deco linear sensibility.
images.altText: Close-up of Umaid Bhawan Palace's central dome and cupola in Chittar sandstone

images.subject: Durbar Hall interior
images.caption: The Durbar Hall, Umaid Bhawan Palace
images.imageDetail: A 150-foot-long ceremonial chamber with gilded ceiling, Czechoslovakian crystal chandeliers, and murals by Stefan Norblin depicting the Ramayana.
images.altText: Durbar Hall at Umaid Bhawan Palace with crystal chandeliers and mythological murals
images.articleInsertionPoint: Architecture section — after floor plan description

02-rambagh-palace-jaipur.title: Rambagh Palace: Jaipur's Jewel — A Palace Hotel Fit for Maharajas

images.subject: Palace from Mughal Gardens
images.caption: Rambagh Palace from the Mughal Gardens, Jaipur
images.imageDetail: Once the residence of Maharaja Sawai Man Singh II, Rambagh Palace's 78 rooms, vast Mughal Gardens, and polo bar make it one of the world's great palace hotels.

03-taj-lake-palace-udaipur.title: Taj Lake Palace: Rajasthan's Floating White Marble Dream

images.subject: Taj Lake Palace on Lake Pichola at sunset
images.caption: Taj Lake Palace, Lake Pichola, Udaipur
images.imageDetail: Built between 1743 and 1746 as Jag Niwas, the palace rises from a four-and-a-half-acre natural rock island in Lake Pichola.
images.altText: Taj Lake Palace floating on Lake Pichola at sunset with Aravalli Hills in background

04-city-palace-udaipur.title: City Palace Udaipur: The Crown of Mewar

images.subject: City Palace complex from Lake Pichola
images.caption: City Palace, Udaipur
images.imageDetail: The largest palace complex in Rajasthan, spanning five acres and comprising eleven interconnected palaces built across four centuries.
images.altText: City Palace Udaipur viewed from Lake Pichola at sunset

images.subject: Mor Chowk (Peacock Courtyard) glass mosaic
images.caption: The Mor Chowk (Peacock Courtyard), City Palace, Udaipur
images.imageDetail: Three peacocks rendered in high-relief glass mosaic represent the seasons of Mewar — summer, monsoon, and winter.
images.altText: Mor Chowk Peacock Courtyard with three glass mosaic peacocks at City Palace Udaipur

05-shiv-niwas-palace-udaipur.title: Shiv Niwas Palace: The Guest Wing of the Maharanas

images.subject: Mor Chowk Peacock Courtyard
images.caption: Mor Chowk, City Palace, Udaipur
images.imageDetail: Hotel guests enjoy exclusive after-hours access to the City Palace courtyards.

06-fateh-prakash-palace-udaipur.title: Fateh Prakash Palace: Crystal, Chandeliers, and the Durbar Hall

images.subject: Durbar Hall interior
images.caption: The Durbar Hall, Fateh Prakash Palace, Udaipur
images.imageDetail: Double-height ceiling with Bohemian crystal chandeliers, arched windows framing Lake Pichola — the finest ceremonial chamber in Udaipur.
images.altText: Durbar Hall at Fateh Prakash Palace with crystal chandeliers and arched windows overlooking Lake Pichola

07-samode-palace-jaipur.title: Samode Palace: The Intimate Rajput Jewel Hidden in the Hills

images.subject: Palace exterior from approach
images.caption: Samode Palace, Jaipur
images.imageDetail: A 475-year-old frescoed masterpiece tucked into the Aravalli Hills — smaller than the grand palace hotels but richer in atmosphere.
images.altText: Samode Palace exterior with golden facade and bougainvillea against Aravalli Hills

08-samode-haveli-jaipur.title: Samode Haveli: The Nobleman's Mansion in Jaipur's Old City

images.subject: Inner courtyard with frescoes
images.caption: Courtyard of Samode Haveli, Jaipur
images.imageDetail: Hand-painted frescoes in vegetable dyes cover every surface, their colours softened by two centuries of Rajasthani sunlight.
images.altText: Inner courtyard of Samode Haveli Jaipur with frescoed walls and fountain

09-raas-jodhpur.title: RAAS Jodhpur: Where Ancient Stone Meets Modern Design Beneath the Fort

images.subject: Mehrangarh Fort exterior
images.caption: Mehrangarh Fort, Jodhpur
images.imageDetail: Built by Rao Jodha in 1459, Mehrangarh is one of India's largest forts — its 118-foot walls rising from a 400-foot basalt cliff define every view from RAAS.
images.altText: Mehrangarh Fort Jodhpur golden sandstone ramparts at sunset

images.subject: Blue City from Mehrangarh Fort
images.caption: The Blue City of Jodhpur from Mehrangarh Fort
images.imageDetail: A sea of indigo-washed houses spreads below the citadel — the blue paint signified Brahmin residences and provided cooling and insect-repelling properties.
images.altText: Blue City Jodhpur viewed from Mehrangarh Fort ramparts
